# Dell SmartFabric OS10 — GUI ↔ CLI ↔ SNMP Mapping

Per [`gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md): the CLI column is the literal command text echoed into the terminal exactly as a human would type it. OS10 is **immediate-apply by default** (see [overview.md](overview.md)) — every row below assumes the default mode, not the opt-in `start transaction` candidate-configuration mode, unless noted. No SNMP write path is confirmed for any action in this table this session (see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)) — every row is CLI-only pending further research, which is itself a finding worth stating plainly rather than leaving implicit.

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `configure terminal`<br>`interface ethernet 1/1/2`<br>`no shutdown` | Not confirmed — treat as CLI-only pending research, per [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)'s standing "not yet researched" status for this vendor's SNMP write surface (unlike the other six Tier-1 vendors, where `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` write support was individually confirmed or ruled out). | `show running-configuration` (interface section) or `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` GET | **Do not assume the near-universal `ifAdminStatus` baseline applies here without checking** — this is the one vendor in this project's full-tier set where even that near-universal object hasn't been individually confirmed. |
| Disable port | `configure terminal`<br>`interface ethernet 1/1/2`<br>`shutdown` | Not confirmed. | Same as above | **On a VLAN (SVI) interface specifically, `shutdown` only stops L3-routed traffic** — L2 traffic keeps passing if the VLAN has no IP configured (confirmed vendor behavior, see [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md)). SignalScope's GUI must not present this as an unconditional "disable" the way it can for every other vendor's `shutdown` — surface the L2-vs-L3 distinction explicitly for VLAN interfaces on this vendor. |
| Configure trunk with tagged + untagged VLANs | `configure terminal`<br>`interface ethernet 1/1/2`<br>`switchport mode trunk`<br>`switchport access vlan 20`<br>`switchport trunk allowed vlan 10` | Not confirmed. | `show running-configuration` (interface section) | Note OS10's distinctive reuse of `switchport access vlan` *inside* trunk mode to mean "the untagged VLAN on this trunk," not "put the port in access mode" — see the flagged caveat in [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md). GUI logic must not treat this command name as an access-mode toggle for this vendor the way it safely can for Cisco/Arista/Aruba. |
| Enable EdgePort (PortFast-equivalent) | `configure terminal`<br>`interface ethernet 1/1/2`<br>`spanning-tree port type edge` | Not confirmed; consistent with every other vendor in this project having no SNMP path for this concept (see [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md)). | `show running-configuration` (interface section) | **CLI-only**, same pattern as all six other Tier-1 vendors. |
| Configure LACP port-channel membership | `configure terminal`<br>`interface port-channel 100`<br>`exit`<br>`interface ethernet 1/1/2`<br>`channel-group 100 mode active` | Not confirmed; consistent with every other vendor (LACP membership is CLI-only everywhere in this project). | `show lacp port-channel` | Note the **inverted sequencing** relative to Cisco/Arista/Huawei: those vendors configure the member interface directly with `channel-group <n> mode active`, implicitly creating the port-channel; OS10's confirmed sequence explicitly creates `interface port-channel 100` first, then references it from each member — the terminal echo must show both steps in this order, not synthesize a single-command equivalent. |
| Enable port security + set MAC limit + violation action | `configure terminal`<br>`interface ethernet 1/1/1`<br>`switchport port-security`<br>`no disable`<br>`mac-learn limit 100`<br>`mac-learn limit violation shutdown` | Not confirmed. | `show switchport port-security` | Five-line CLI sequence (enter port-security sub-context, explicitly un-disable it, set limit, set violation action) — the longest confirmed multi-step action for this vendor. Note `shutdown` violation puts the interface in **error-disable** status specifically (not plain admin-down) — GUI should render this as a distinct state, matching how Huawei's port-security shutdown and other vendors' error-disable states are typically surfaced. |
| Save / persist configuration | `write memory` | Not confirmed. `CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB`-style RowStatus-driven config-copy MIB (the pattern confirmed genuine for both Cisco and Aruba, see [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md)) was not searched for specifically on Dell this session — worth checking in a follow-up pass given the pattern's recurrence across two other vendors. | `show running-configuration` vs. last-known startup-config diff (config-drift tier) | Persist-only semantics, same category as Cisco/Arista/Huawei/Aruba's base case (see [comparison/cli-syntax-matrix.md](../../comparison/cli-syntax-matrix.md)) — running-config is already live, this just writes it to startup-config. |
| Guarded/staged apply (candidate-configuration mode) | `start transaction`<br>*(config commands staged, not applied)*<br>`commit` (or `discard`) | N/A — this is a CLI session behavior, not a single object write, same as Aruba's `checkpoint auto <n>` and Junos's `commit`. | `show candidate-configuration` / `show diff candidate-configuration running-configuration` | Distinct GUI concept from plain Save, available only when SignalScope explicitly opens a transaction-mode session — see [overview.md](overview.md)'s config-apply model discussion for the full architectural framing (structurally between Aruba's opt-in safety-net checkpoint and Junos's mandatory candidate/commit). |
| Configure an SNMPv3 user | `configure terminal`<br>`snmp-server user <user> <group> <security-model> auth sha <pass> priv aes <pass>` | N/A — configuring the SNMP agent's own access control cannot itself be done via SNMP (same chicken-and-egg limitation as every vendor in this project). | `show snmp user` | CLI-only by necessity. |
| Configure an SNMP trap host | `configure terminal`<br>`snmp-server host 10.0.0.5 traps version 2c public` | N/A, same reasoning. | `show running-configuration` (SNMP section, exact show-command for trap-host read-back not independently confirmed this session) | CLI-only by necessity. |

## Summary for SignalScope's capability matrix

Every action in this table is **CLI-only**. **Updated Phase 2 (2026-07-22)**: this is no longer purely a research gap the way it was in the original pass — a first-hand read of Dell's complete OS10 MIB list (see [`mib-reference.md`](mib-reference.md) and [`overview.md`](overview.md)) confirmed that **none of OS10's five enterprise MIBs is a configuration-action module** (no equivalent of Cisco's `CISCO-VLAN-MEMBERSHIP-MIB`/`CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` or Aruba's port-security/config/MSTP MIBs exists at all), which rules out an entire category of possible write paths rather than just leaving them unchecked. What remains genuinely unconfirmed (not ruled out) is narrower: whether the standard `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid`/`IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` objects accept a live SET on OS10 hardware — this would need a live device to resolve and, even if eventually confirmed, wouldn't change the CLI-only guidance for any other action in this table (trunk-VLAN, STP edge-port, port-security, LACP, config-save all have no supporting MIB, documented or otherwise). Dell's SNMP-write evidence is now **more thoroughly negative than Huawei's** (which has one confirmed positive, PVID write) rather than merely thinner — a materially different, and more useful, status for implementers than "not yet researched."
